skill.name: gemini-computer-use
skill.description: Build and run a Gemini Computer Use browser-control agent with Playwright. The skill supports screenshot loops, Gemini function calls, action execution, and safety confirmations.
skill.summary: Run Gemini Computer Use browser automation loops with Playwright.
skill.author: am-will

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are scanner noise: empty environment templates, Markdown code fences, and keyboard actions misclassified as certificate access. Real risks remain because the skill sends browser screenshots to Gemini, loads external pages, reads a user API key, and executes model-selected browser actions. I found no prompt-injection language in the reviewed skill text.

remediation.issue: Model-directed browser actions execute with limited gating.
remediation.suggestion: Require an explicit action allowlist, domain allowlist, and confirmation for high-impact actions even when the model omits safety_decision.

remediation.issue: Browser screenshots are sent to Gemini.
remediation.suggestion: Warn users before authenticated browsing, redact sensitive pages where possible, and avoid logging screenshots or URLs.

remediation.issue: Environment variables can select a browser executable path.
remediation.suggestion: Validate COMPUTER_USE_BROWSER_EXECUTABLE against trusted paths, or remove this option for marketplace distribution.

remediation.issue: The API key is sourced from the shell environment.
remediation.suggestion: Keep env.sh ignored by git, never print the key, and document secret handling clearly.

semantic_findings.title: Model-Directed Browser Actions
semantic_findings.description: The loop executes function calls from Gemini for navigation, clicks, typing, key combinations, scrolling, and drag actions. Confirmation only occurs when a model-provided safety_decision asks for it.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code directly maps Gemini function_call names and arguments to Playwright actions. The confirmation gate depends on the call arguments containing safety_decision.

semantic_findings.title: Screenshots Sent To External Model
semantic_findings.description: The script captures browser screenshots and includes them in Gemini requests and function responses. Screenshots can contain sensitive page data during authenticated browsing.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code captures screenshot bytes, attaches them to model content, and calls generate_content. This is a clear data-flow path to Google GenAI.

semantic_findings.title: Environment-Controlled Browser Executable
semantic_findings.description: The script reads COMPUTER_USE_BROWSER_EXECUTABLE and passes it to Playwright as executable_path. A compromised environment can redirect browser launch to an untrusted local binary.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The env var is read directly and assigned to launch_options before Playwright launches Chromium. Exploitability depends on environment control, so confidence is high but not absolute.

content.value_statement: Browser automation with vision models is hard to wire safely. This skill provides a Playwright loop for Gemini Computer Use actions and confirmations.
actual_capabilities: Provides setup steps for Python, Playwright, google-genai, and browser installation.
Runs Gemini 2.5 Computer Use with a screenshot and function-call loop.
Launches a Playwright Chromium browser with configurable URL, viewport, and headless mode.
Executes browser actions including navigation, clicks, typing, scrolling, and drag actions.
Prompts for user confirmation when Gemini returns a safety decision requiring confirmation.
Supports repeated excluded-action settings through the --exclude option.
limitations: Requires a Gemini API key and network access to Google GenAI.
Executes browser actions requested by the model, so sandboxing is important.
Supports browser automation through Playwright, not desktop applications outside the browser.
Uses a preview model name, so provider behavior and availability can change.

output_examples.input: Run a basic site inspection task on a public page.
output_examples.output: The agent opens the page, inspects visible content, reports the main result, and stops after the turn limit or final answer.

output_examples.input: Review whether the browser agent is ready for an authenticated workflow.
output: Use a sandboxed browser profile before signing in.
Exclude key combinations and drag actions unless they are required.
Confirm how screenshots and URLs are handled before entering sensitive data.

output_examples.input: Add action limits for a read-only research task.
output_examples.output: The recommended setup keeps navigation, waiting, and scrolling available while excluding typing, key combinations, and drag actions.

best_practices: Run the browser in a sandboxed profile or container for every test session.
Use --exclude to remove actions that the current task does not require.
Keep the Gemini API key in the environment and do not commit local env files.
anti_patterns: Running the agent on production accounts without a review step.
Allowing unrestricted typing, key combinations, or drag actions for sensitive workflows.
Saving screenshots, URLs, logs, or environment files that contain private data.

faq.question: Does this skill include a working agent script?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes a Python script that connects Gemini Computer Use with a Playwright browser loop.

faq.question: Which model does the script target?
faq.answer: The script targets the Gemini 2.5 Computer Use preview model listed in the source.

faq.question: Does it require an API key?
faq.answer: Yes. The script reads GEMINI_API_KEY from the environment before creating the Google GenAI client.

faq.question: Can it run without showing a browser window?
faq.answer: Yes. The script supports a headless mode through its command-line option.

faq.question: Does it automatically block risky actions?
faq.answer: It asks for confirmation only when Gemini returns a safety decision. Use action exclusions for stronger control.

faq.question: Can it automate desktop applications?
faq.answer: No. The included implementation is limited to browser automation through Playwright.
